notes:
WHAT THE NUMBERS MEAN
Wall time includes HTTP and stream completion. TTFT ends at the first content or reasoning delta.
Chunk gaps are not exact token latency: a chunk may hold several tokens.
TPOT proxy = (last - first generation arrival) / (completion_tokens - 1).
Decode proxy = its inverse. Prefill proxy = prompt_tokens / TTFT, so it includes queueing,
tokenizing and the first decode step.
Phases come from the engine's own /profile, one row per turn. Engine counters come from its log.
Requests are sequential and shuffled each round. Warmups and failures are left out of statistics.
Each request has a unique prefix to limit prefix reuse. A few repetitions give limited confidence.

GPU IN-FLIGHT PERCENT
Time with at least one job between "handed to the GuC" and "fence signalled", from xe tracepoints.
It includes GuC scheduling and time other VFs held the engine, so it is an upper bound on how busy
the EUs were, not an EU utilization. It cannot separate XMX from EU work.

MICROBENCHMARKS (vkprobe)
Active load through Vulkan with the engine's own Mesa, run while the engine is idle. VRAM buffers
hold random data so Battlemage's compression cannot flatter them. xmx_* rates from registers show
what the matrix units can do; the from-memory rates show what a shader reloading operands gets.

PROFILING COST (decode speed against Light, measured on this machine, 6 requests each)
Light            /proc, gateway, xpu-smi                 no measurable cost
Standard         + xe job trace, CPU hotspots            -6%
Deep             + perf stat on the engine (IPC, misses) -23%
perf stat is the expensive one: the engine switches context about 9000 times a second, and on a VM
each switch with PMU counters active traps to the hypervisor. So take speed from Light runs and
reasons from Standard or Deep runs, and only compare runs of the same level.

HYPERVISOR COUNTERS CHANGE THE ENGINE TOO, THE OTHER WAY
With hostagent.py streaming, decode runs about 19% faster (measured, 6 requests each): xpu-smi
polling the GPU accounts for about 16%, the xe PMU's engine counters for about 11%; host CPU and
uncore counters had no effect. Both touch the GPU's firmware. The clock barely moves during decode
(about 1200-1350 MHz either way), so the likely cause is the GPU leaving idle states less often
between decode's short jobs. That mechanism is not confirmed yet. So the live hypervisor stream runs at Standard and Deep only,
never at Light, and a run that had it is marked. The hypervisor's configuration snapshot is a
one-off read and is always taken.
